MESA CORE v0.8.1 · INSIDE THE ENGINE

How information moves through MESA.

The architecture has two main paths: turning a source into stored memory, and finding evidence when an application asks a question. Follow both paths below, from entry to output.

01 · Write information ↓02 · Find information ↓03 · See the building blocks ↓

THE WHOLE SYSTEM AT A GLANCE

One application outside. One storage owner inside.

In the supported V4 topology, one combined process owns the API admission path, background consumers and all three stores. The boxes below are responsibilities inside that process, not separate servers.

01 · THE WRITE PATH

From exact source text to usable memory.

Your application provides exact text and its document, revision and chunk identity. Core consumes that source; source acquisition and chunk preparation belong to the producer.

  1. 01

    Check the session and source

    The server derives access scope from the authenticated session. The request identifies a dataset, document, revision and exact source chunk.

    POST /v4/memory/insert
  2. 02

    Accept the work durably

    A candidate, mutation ledger record and pipeline run are created. HTTP 202 confirms admission; it does not confirm completed processing.

    MemoryCandidate · memory_mutations · pipeline_runs
  3. 03

    Extract structured facts

    FactExtractionService uses a model to extract zero or more subject–relation–object facts, keeping the link to the supporting text.

    FactExtractionService → 0..N FactCandidate
  4. 04

    Apply the selected validation

    Mode 0 uses deterministic checks; mode 1 adds one model validator; mode 2 requires two distinct provider/model pairs to agree. These checks gate admission to active memory.

    MESA_TIER3_MODE = 0 / 1 / 2
  5. 05

    Write the stores in order

    Canonical facts are written to SQLite, then vector representations to LanceDB, then relationships to Kùzu. Each stage waits for its predecessor.

    SQL → vector → graph
  6. 06

    Confirm completion

    The client checks the durable mutation status. COMMITTED is the successful terminal state; an accepted request alone is not enough.

    COMMITTED
Pipeline statesQUEUED → RUNNING → EXTRACTED → VALIDATED → PROJECTING → COMMITTED

The pipeline summarizes progress; the mutation ledger tracks the SQL_APPLIED, VECTOR_APPLIED and GRAPH_APPLIED write stages separately.

WHERE DOES EACH PIECE LIVE?

The record is authoritative. Search views follow it.

SQLite owns documents, immutable revisions, entities, assertions, permissions and processing state. FTS5 also supplies keyword search over passages and evidence.

LanceDB: find similar meaning
Stores derived assertion vectors. The query representation must use the compatible embedding model and dimensions.
Kùzu: follow relationships
Stores derived entities and assertion edges. A graph path must reconcile to eligible canonical assertions.
ILLUSTRATIVE FACT + SOURCE

Atlas archive → weekday opening time → 09:00

Visitor guide → revision 1 → chunk 1 → supporting passage

02 · THE READ PATH

From a question to source-linked evidence.

The session fixes the authorized datasets. Tenant, dataset, agent, committed-state and applicable time/jurisdiction rules constrain candidates before rank contribution. MemoryDAO.search_v4_memory coordinates the search.

Search returns evidence

Hits retain assertion, document, revision, chunk and retrieval-origin identity. A bounded graph path retains its supporting assertions and directions.

ContextBuilder fits the model’s input

The context endpoint packs evidence once into a token budget, defaulting to 2048 formatted-evidence tokens. Complete graph proof must fit together; the application model then writes the answer.

Optional adaptive search: when is the question reformulated?

Search and context default to a single query. When adaptive context is explicitly requested, an empty result or insufficient multi-lane support can trigger one planner call and up to two reformulations. Every search keeps the original scope; this does not generate an answer.

Ranking formula and search limits

WHAT IF A STEP FAILS?

Progress is recorded. Recovery follows ownership.

The three stores do not share a single database transaction. Durable work records, expiring ownership leases and idempotent receipts let the system retry or reconcile unfinished work without treating it as success.

VALIDATION REJECTIONREJECTED

Audit source may remain, but no active retrieval artifact is created.

TRANSIENT FAILURERETRY_PENDING → DLQ

Retries are bounded. Exhausted work can enter a dead-letter state rather than loop forever.

ROLLBACK / CLEANUPROLLED_BACK / BLOCKED

Rollback removes that source’s ownership. Shared artifacts survive while another active owner exists; unfinished cleanup stays blocked.

03 · HOW THE CODE IS ASSEMBLED

Separate modules, explicit responsibilities.

mesa_api / mesa_mcp

Entry points

Receive HTTP or MCP requests and bind them to an authenticated session.

mesa_workers

Background work

Consume durable ingestion, projection and maintenance work.

mesa_memory

Information processing

Own extraction, validation, embeddings and context building.

mesa_storage

Records and search

Own canonical SQLite state, source ownership, projections and retrieval through MemoryDAO.

mesa_client

Application connection

Provides synchronous and asynchronous Python clients for the HTTP boundary.

General dependency directionAPI / MCP → workers → memory → storage

Runtime composition roots are explicit exceptions to that layering. MemoryDAO is the compatibility façade; mesa_evals supplies diagnostics and retrieval contract tooling outside the request path.
